title: Official Amazon page defining the ASIN - located
detail: The definition was located on Amazon's own publishing surface: "ASIN" stands for "Amazon Standard Identification Number". It's a unique 10-character alphanumeric code assigned to every product listed in the Amazon store, and the page adds that the ASIN appears after "/dp/" in a product URL. Registered as S27 (https://sell.amazon.com/blog/what-is-an-asin, read 2026-11-20, page dated Jun 4, 2025) and cited wherever this site explains why the intended-ASIN field is blank. S25 (Seller Central help G1471) is kept as the page that lists ASIN among accepted product identifiers.
owner_status: Resolved 2026-11-20. The blank intended-ASIN field is now anchored to an official definition.

title: Supplied tokens are 9 characters; Amazon defines an ASIN as 10
detail: All five link.amazon path tokens (B04G1MEwY, B02NbDxp3, B00hJ57DV, B0c8moW59, B0f3GKalj) are 9 characters, while the resolved ASINs are 10. Amazon's own definition settles the question: an ASIN is a unique 10-character alphanumeric code assigned to every product in the store (S27, read 2026-11-20). A 9-character token therefore cannot be an ASIN - it is a short-link code - so the intended-ASIN fields stay blank (FLG-001) and the observed redirect target remains the only identifier this site has verified. Supersedes the earlier wording of FLG-014, which asserted the same finding without an official source to anchor it.
owner_status: Published on the Flagged for Review page. Owner: supply the intended ASIN per product (FLG-001).
